clue.text: Regroup in large formation

indicators.note: a formation is an arrangement, so the letters of in large are drawn up in a new order

explanation.surface: An instruction to a big army to form up again in a single large formation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'formation' tells you to rearrange the letters of IN LARGE.
explanation.definitionFit: To regroup is to line things up again in fresh positions, a synonym.

clue.text: Soldier with interest in wanting to live

parts.note: RE, the Royal Engineers, stands for a soldier in crosswords
a side is a party or interest group in a dispute

explanation.surface: A soldier with a stake in something who is desperate to stay alive.
explanation.walkthrough: RE (Royal Engineers) is a stock crossword soldier; SIDE is an interest in the sense of a faction or party. 'with' and 'in wanting to' only link the pieces to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To reside somewhere is to dwell or have one's home there, a synonym of live.

clue.text: He's far out once more

indicators.note: out signals that the letters of He's far are put out of their usual order

parts.note: taken as written, the apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: Someone has gone far away yet again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges HESFAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something afresh means starting again from the beginning, a synonym of once more.

clue.text: Rashness and cheek? That's about right

indicators.note: about means going round, so the word for cheek is placed around the letter for right

explanation.surface: Someone remarks that being rash and cheeky is pretty much accurate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts IMPUDENCE (cheek) around R (right); 'That's' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: Imprudence is a lack of caution or good judgement, which is what rashness means.

clue.text: Part of church left for contemplation

definitions.note: the definition is a descriptive phrase: the belly button is the classic thing gazed at in contemplation

parts.note: the nave is the main body of a church

explanation.surface: A section of a church set aside for quiet prayer and reflection.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on navel-gazing, staring at one's belly button in deep thought.
explanation.definitionFit: Navel-gazing is the idiom for self-absorbed thinking, so the belly button is the object of contemplation.

clue.text: The wishes of a worshipful company

definitions.text: The wishes of a worshipful company

parts.words: The wishes of a worshipful company
parts.note: a Worshipful Company is a London livery guild, but read literally it is a congregation at worship, and its wishes are what it asks of God

explanation.surface: What one of the City of London's ancient livery companies would like.
explanation.walkthrough: The Worshipful Companies are the old trade guilds of the City of London; the clue reads the phrase literally as people at worship.
explanation.definitionFit: Requests addressed to God by worshippers are the wishes of a congregation.

clue.text: A case for the papers

parts.note: sounds like a story fit for the newspapers, but means a flat carrying case for loose documents

explanation.surface: A scandal that the newspapers ought to cover.
explanation.definitionFit: A portfolio is a flat folder or case for carrying documents or drawings.

clue.text: Turning point in a revolution

parts.note: sounds like a decisive moment in a political uprising, but means the rod round which a wheel spins

explanation.surface: The decisive moment in a political uprising.
explanation.definitionFit: A wheel rotates about its central shaft, the pivot of each turn.

clue.text: Useful for cracking the surface before a dip at breakfast time

definitions.text: Useful for cracking the surface before a dip at breakfast time

parts.words: Useful for cracking the surface before a dip at breakfast time
parts.note: describes a small utensil that taps open a boiled shell before toast soldiers are dipped into the yolk

explanation.surface: Something handy for breaking the ice before a morning swim.
explanation.definitionFit: A small spoon for eating a boiled egg is used to break its shell before dipping in.

clue.text: Inundated with State Aid, perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps hints that the letters of State Aid may be a disguised version of something else

explanation.surface: Someone or something swamped with government handouts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges STATEAID.
explanation.definitionFit: Being sated or glutted means having been flooded with more than enough, a figurative synonym.

clue.text: Traditionally it was applied to the back parts

indicators.note: sending the word parts to the back means reading it from its rear end forwards

explanation.surface: A remark about old-fashioned corporal punishment applied to a pupil's rear.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes a leather belt used to beat schoolchildren; 'to the back' reverses PARTS.
explanation.definitionFit: A leather belt was the instrument formerly used for corporal punishment in schools.

clue.text: Brilliant featherweight?

explanation.surface: A boxer in the featherweight division who is outstanding.
explanation.walkthrough: A Very light is a coloured signal flare fired from a pistol, named after its inventor Edward Very.
explanation.definitionFit: A Very flare blazes brightly in the sky, and something weighing almost nothing is extremely slight in heft.

clue.text: Exclude underworld leader with pass

parts.note: Dis is the Roman god who rules the underworld
to pass a test is to qualify

explanation.surface: A gangland boss is barred despite holding a permit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'underworld leader' suggests a crime boss, but it is Dis, Roman ruler of the dead.
explanation.definitionFit: To disqualify someone is to bar them from taking part, a synonym of exclude.

clue.text: Heap makes a bushel

indicators.note: makes signals that the letters of Heap are made into another word

explanation.surface: A pile of grain amounts to a bushel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'makes' rearranges HEAP into an old Hebrew dry measure.
explanation.definitionFit: The ephah was an ancient Hebrew dry measure of roughly a bushel.

clue.text: Tornado over the sea that takes the rain away!

explanation.surface: A storm at sea that carries off the rainfall.
explanation.definitionFit: A whirling column of cloud and spray over the ocean, and also a gutter pipe that carries off rainwater from a roof.

clue.text: Don't try to improve on a perfectly good water supply

explanation.surface: Advice not to tinker with a sound source of water.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition splits the phrase into let, well, alone: leave a good well by itself.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means leave something satisfactory untouched, and a sound shaft sunk for water needs no interference.

clue.text: Wants deal arranged for barren area

indicators.note: arranged means the letters of Wants deal are set out in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone wants a deal set up for some unproductive land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arranged' rearranges WANTSDEAL.
explanation.definitionFit: A wasteland is desolate land where nothing grows, a synonym.

clue.text: A spot of capital punishment

parts.note: sounds like a small dose of execution, but spot means place: the platform where hangings were carried out

explanation.surface: A little bit of the death penalty.
explanation.definitionFit: The raised platform for public hanging or beheading was the place of execution.

clue.text: With fashion, price is not extreme

parts.note: mode is a style or fashion
a rate is a price charged

explanation.surface: Fashionable goods at a reasonable price.
explanation.definitionFit: Moderate means middling or within reasonable limits, the opposite of excessive.

clue.text: Buyer of an electric fan?

parts.note: someone who buys a cooling device is literally a chilly shopper, but the phrase is idiom for an unflappable person

explanation.surface: A shopper purchasing a cooling appliance.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes a calm, unruffled person, here read literally as a chilled shopper.

clue.text: Old crone gets leg broken into the bargain

parts.note: a hag is an ugly old woman

indicators.note: broken signals that the letters of leg are smashed into a new order

explanation.surface: An old woman breaks her leg on top of everything else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broken' turns LEG into GLE. 'into the bargain' looks like the idiom meaning besides, but bargain is the definition, a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To haggle is to argue over a price, which is what bargaining means as a verb.

clue.text: Changes which should be made by wrongdoers

definitions.text: which should be made by wrongdoers

explanation.surface: Alterations that those who have done wrong ought to carry out.
explanation.definitionFit: Amends as a verb means alters, and making amends is compensating for harm done.

clue.text: Went so hurriedly, left without having eaten

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside: the word for having eaten sits outside the letter for left

explanation.surface: Someone rushed off and departed without stopping for a meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like plain lacking, but here it is the old word for outside, so FED goes around L.
explanation.definitionFit: To flee is to run away in haste, so its past tense means went in a hurry.

clue.text: Extra space may be mensurable

indicators.note: may be hints that mensurable, rearranged, could become another word

explanation.surface: Additional room might be capable of being measured.
explanation.walkthrough: 'may be' rearranges MENSURABLE into the German word for living space.
explanation.definitionFit: The German term for living room sought by a nation to expand territorially, so additional territory.

clue.text: Incident on Orient Express?

parts.note: the Orient is the East, abbreviated E
to vent feelings is to express them

explanation.surface: Something happens aboard the famous Orient Express train.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface evokes the luxury train; 'on' simply joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: An event is a happening or occurrence, a synonym of incident.

clue.text: Indian city flag raised around site of the Taj Mahal

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Indian city flag raised around site of the Taj Mahal'; no reading of 'flag raised around' gives the letters, so the wordplay part looks garbled or misread
annotationWithheld.clue: Indian city flag raised around site of the Taj Mahal

clue.text: For a drink, agreed on a cocktail

indicators.note: a cocktail is a mixture, so the letters of agreed on a are shaken up

explanation.surface: Friends settle on a mixed drink to order.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cocktail' looks like the drink but is the anagram signal for AGREEDONA; 'For' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: Orangeade is a sweet soft beverage flavoured with citrus juice.

clue.text: Newspaper in the loft?

explanation.surface: A newspaper lying up in the attic.
explanation.walkthrough: The organ loft is the gallery in a church where the pipe instrument stands; 'loft' suggests an attic.
explanation.definitionFit: A journal acting as a mouthpiece for a party, and the pipe instrument housed in a church gallery.

clue.text: Being obstinate, had dire trouble

indicators.note: trouble means disturbance, so the letters of had dire are stirred up

explanation.surface: Someone stubborn found themselves in serious difficulty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trouble' rearranges HADDIRE.
explanation.definitionFit: Die-hard describes someone stubbornly resisting change, a synonym of obstinate.

clue.text: Ties the rest in knots

indicators.note: tied in knots means tangled, so the letters of the rest are muddled up

explanation.surface: Someone binds up everything else with knots.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in knots' rearranges THEREST.
explanation.definitionFit: Tethers are ropes that fasten an animal, and as a verb it means binds, like ties.
